description: An interactive space survival game inspired by NASA missions, where players act as astronauts or base managers on the Moon or Mars. They must build and manage a sustainable base by balancing essential resources such as oxygen, water, energy, food, and radiation protection. Players face unexpected space emergencies, equipment failures, and environmental challenges that require quick decisions and effective problem-solving. The goal is to ensure the crew's survival and create a self-sustaining.
summary: ZATHURA is an Arabic-first educational space game built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 (The Next Frontier) in the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer category, aimed at ages 7–12. A single launcher opens two modes that share one commander and one story. Outpost is a strategic base simulator on Canvas 2D: six destinations (Moon, Mars, Mercury, Venus, Saturn/Titan, and the fictional planet Zewail), five power-hungry systems competing over one budget, local resource utilisation (ice → water and oxygen, regolith → shielding), and a career radiation dose of 600 mSv that never resets. Odyssey: Survive is a first-person 3D rescue mission (React 19 + Three.js) inside a spacecraft, with eight disaster types and six landing sites. Every constant comes from published NASA data — BVAD 2022 and ECLSS life-support figures, RAD/MSL dose rates, and the May 2024 DONKI solar archive — and each one is explicitly labelled NASA data or game estimate. It runs offline, with no install and no server, from self-contained HTML files. One design idea drives it: time and dose are the two resources you can never earn back, and every decision carries a written price — so the lesson is that exploration is a sequence of deliberate trade-offs, not a power fantasy.
details: ZATHURA is an Arabic-first educational space game for ages 7–12, built for the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge. One launcher opens two games sharing one commander and story: Outpost, a strategic base simulator across six destinations where 24 crew-hours per Sol must cover digging, analysis, repairs and rest while five systems compete for one power budget and radiation accumulates against a 600 mSv career ceiling that never resets; and Odyssey: Survive, a first-person 3D rescue mission (React 19 + Three.js) with eight disaster types and six landing sites. Children manufacture water, oxygen and shielding from local ice and regolith (ISRU), driven by 36 adaptive scenarios that explain why each outcome happened. Constants come from published NASA data — ECLSS, BVAD 2022, RAD/MSL and a cached May 2024 DONKI storm archive — each labelled "NASA data" or "game estimate" among 22 attributed sources. Mode 1 is vanilla JavaScript on Canvas 2D with Web Audio and a dependency-free Node build; Mode 2 uses React 19, TypeScript, Vite and Three.js. It runs offline with no install on any modern browser, keyboard or touch.
dataRefs: NASA Data & Resources NASA Open APIs: NASA's central public API portal, providing free programmatic access to datasets including the Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD), Mars Rover Photos, and the Space Weather Database (DONKI). A free API key (higher rate limits than the shared demo key) can be requested instantly and is a good starting point for any challenge team building a data-connected prototype.  Space Weather Database Of Notifications, Knowledge, Information (DONKI): Real, regularly updated data on solar flares, coronal mass ejections, and other space weather events that drive radiation risk for astronauts and spacecraft. Useful for grounding any radiation-shielding, communications-disruption, or mission-risk mechanic in actual current conditions rather than invented numbers.  NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR): (search API) NASA's public archive of space biology and astronaut health research, including studies on how spaceflight affects bone density, muscle mass, immune response, sleep, and more across many organisms. Searchable by keyword, making it well suited for tools that want to surface real published NASA science relevant to human health trade-offs in space.  RadLab (OSDR Radiation Dosimetry Database): Real radiation dose measurements recorded by dosimetry instruments aboard the International Space Station, contributed by multiple international space agencies. Provides authentic astronaut radiation exposure data (e.g., absorbed dose rate) useful for any tool modeling shielding, health risk, or long-duration mission trade-offs.  Mars Trek: An interactive visualization and data-download portal for real Mars surface imagery, elevation, and terrain data compiled from NASA's Mars missions (including Curiosity and Perseverance). Useful for teams wanting real environmental or geographic data to ground a Mars outpost site or terrain visualization in actual surface conditions.

projectRefs: Space Agency Partner Resources CSA (Canadian Space Agency)  Space resources for STEM and youth organizations: The CSA's Space Resources for STEM and Youth Organizations page provides free, bilingual tools and activities to help educators engage youth in space and STEM. Designed for museums, libraries, camps, after-school clubs, community groups, and outreach organizations, these resources support learning beyond the classroom.  Food production on the moon and in remote areas: This web package is a one-stop resource for educators and youth who want to learn about food in space. This toolkit aims to outline how food production in space can relate to the health and nutrition of astronauts as well as benefit humans on Earth.
